myths.text: Kǒngzǐ is attested in the canonical Chinese sources as a figure associated with confucius, moral teaching, ritual.

myths.title: Name and Meaning
myths.text: The name means "Master Kong" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition.

lore.syncretism: Kǒngzǐ appears within the Chinese tradition and has influenced later retellings, artistic depictions, and scholarly study. The Unicode restoration preserves the name's distinctive orthography for contemporary use.
lore.culturalLegacy: Kǒngzǐ continues to appear in scholarship, art, and popular reception as a significant figure of the Chinese tradition. Restoring the name in Unicode returns the original marks that ASCII removes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Kǒngzǐ embodies confucius, moral teaching, ritual in the Chinese imagination. The name's restoration is not merely cosmetic: it recovers the stress, length, and script that make the figure recognizable in the source tradition.
lore.archaeology: Kǒngzǐ is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Chinese tradition.
